rationale: Create one canonical Salamanca Infrastructure LLC record for ArcLight's Salamanca census holding. The active Delaware company owns the Salamanca floating production system and associated oil and natural-gas export laterals at Keathley Canyon Block 689 in the deepwater U.S. Gulf of Mexico. Count this infrastructure once; exclude the separate Leon and Castile upstream fields, wells and leases, the former Independence Hub identity, LLOG as operator, and the subordinate Salamanca Infrastructure Finance, Salamanca FPS Infra and Salamanca OGL Infra entities. ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII-backed affiliates financed the development through an ownership arrangement and hold a plurality ownership interest; the exact percentage and legal investment vehicle are not publicly disclosed. Repsol completed a combined 20% sale to ArcLight and Centaurus in December 2023 and retained 2.5%, but public sources do not disclose the complete current capitalization table or allocation of the sold interest. ArcLight continues to list Salamanca as Current, and no ArcLight exit or signed pending Salamanca sale was identified through August 15, 2026.

afterImage.name: Salamanca Infrastructure LLC
afterImage.subsector: Offshore floating production and export infrastructure
afterImage.description: Salamanca Infrastructure LLC is the U.S. midstream infrastructure owner of the Salamanca floating production system and associated oil and natural-gas export laterals at Keathley Canyon Block 689 in the deepwater U.S. Gulf of Mexico. The refurbished semi-submersible receives production from the separate Leon and Castile upstream fields and can process 60,000 barrels of oil per day and 40 million cubic feet of natural gas per day. LLOG operates the facility but is not treated as a manager-level owner. ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII-backed affiliates financed the development through an ownership arrangement and hold a plurality ownership interest; the exact ArcLight percentage and legal investment vehicle are not publicly disclosed. Repsol completed a combined 20% sale to ArcLight and Centaurus in December 2023 and reported a retained 2.5% direct interest at year-end 2025. Public sources do not disclose a complete current capitalization table. The Leon and Castile fields, wells and leases and the subordinate Salamanca Infrastructure Finance, Salamanca FPS Infra and Salamanca OGL Infra entities are not separate PortCos. No ArcLight exit or signed pending Salamanca sale was identified through August 15, 2026.
afterImage.headquarters: Keathley Canyon Block 689, U.S. Gulf of Mexico

milestones.event: Salamanca Infrastructure LLC was formed as a Delaware limited liability company.

LLOG announced the Salamanca development and an ownership and construction-financing arrangement with ArcLight-managed investment vehicles for the floating production system and associated export laterals.

Repsol completed the combined sale of a 20% Salamanca Infrastructure interest to ArcLight and Centaurus for $129 million and retained a 2.5% interest; the allocation between the purchasers was not disclosed.
The Salamanca floating production unit achieved first production from the Leon field, bringing the refurbished 60,000-barrel-per-day oil and 40-million-cubic-feet-per-day gas facility into operation.
